inline_comments.comment:
The JSDoc says `text` performs an **exact match** for strings, but the implementation on line 59 uses `content.includes(text)`, which is a **substring match**. This means `expect(el).toHaveLiveRegion({ text: 'passed' })` would match a region containing `'3 tests passed, 0 failed'`, potentially producing false-positive test results.

Either correct the documentation to say "substring match", or change the implementation to use `content === text` (or `content.trim() === text`) for true exact matching.

The failure diagnostic only reads the raw `aria-live` attribute, showing `[aria-live="(implicit)"]` for elements whose live-region behaviour comes from a role (e.g. `role="alert"` → assertive, `role="status"` → polite). This hides the effective politeness level and makes it harder to debug failures.

Consider reusing the same `effectiveLevel` inference logic already present in the matching loop to produce a richer label such as `[role="alert" (assertive)]`.

`toHaveLiveRegion` is a Vitest custom matcher — a test-only utility that is meaningful only when called inside `expect.extend()`. Exporting it from the production `storybook/internal/components` module (and, consequently, registering it as a manager global in `exports.ts`) bundles test code into the production Storybook manager. At minimum this increases the production bundle size unnecessarily; if the matcher is tree-shaken away in practice it is still a leaky abstraction.

Consider moving it to a dedicated test-utilities package (e.g. `storybook/internal/test-utils` or alongside the vitest addon's test helpers) and importing it from there in stories and unit tests, keeping the production components module free of test-only exports.

general_comments.comment: The three new stories (`AnnouncesTestRunStart`, `AnnouncesTestRunFinished`, `AnnouncesTestRunCrashed`) are not tagged with `'vitest'`, despite the PR description explicitly stating they are "Tagged with `vitest` for vitest-only test execution." Without the tag, these stories will be picked up by all test runners and may behave unexpectedly in environments that do not support the `announce` / DOM live-region mechanics (e.g. the browser-based test runner). Add `tags: ['vitest']` to each story (or to the meta if appropriate).

`code/core/src/components/components/LiveRegion/LiveRegion.tsx` contains no JSX — it is purely re-exports of imperative functions and a type alias. The `.tsx` extension signals to both the compiler and readers that the file contains React elements, which is misleading. Renaming it to `LiveRegion.ts` aligns the extension with the actual content and avoids unnecessary JSX transform overhead.
